## Review of the new early endpoint proof

The new endpoint is A=x sqrt(N)/2 rather than x sqrt(N/2). For N>0 the new endpoint is below the floored wall, so a nonempty strip still implies S_j≥A. The actual source proves this through sqrt(N)/2≤sqrt(N/2) and monotonicity of the square root. It does not weaken the output theorem or its support assumption.

In `hEarlyEndpoint`, j>0 and 160000j≤N imply N>0 and y=N/j≥160000. For x≥16, x²≥256. Support200 yields B≤B0=sqrt(N)/(200x). The proof correctly derives 24B≤A. It also derives 3sqrt(j)≤A; indeed A²=x²N/4≥64N≥9j, with both sides nonnegative. These are exactly the endpoint-tail head's two guards.

`hLogRatio` proves the needed monotonicity without assuming a missing API. For 0<u≤v, the pinned tangent bound gives `log(1+v)-log(1+u)≤(v-u)/(1+u)`, while the inverse tangent bound gives `u/(1+u)≤log(1+u)`. Multiplying by u and v-u respectively yields `u log(1+v)≤v log(1+u)`. Division by the positive u,v gives the stated decreasing ratio. Its use with u=AB/j and v=AB0/j has the correct direction, since the exponent is to be lower-bounded before negating it.

The exact algebra in the source is AB0/j=y/400 and A/(72B0)=(25/18)x². Because y≥160000, sqrt(y)≥400 and sqrt(y)≤y/400. Thus `log(1+y/400)≥log(y)/2`. The source also proves log(y)≥8 from exp(8)≤3^8=6561≤y. Consequently the Bennett exponent is at least `(25/36)x² log(y)`, which is at least `2x²+log(y)` for x²≥256 and log(y)≥8. One explicit check is

`((25/36)x²−1)log(y) ≥ 8((25/36)x²−1) ≥ 2x²`.

All factors multiplied in these comparisons have the nonnegative/positive guards provided in the source. Exponentiating the negative inequality gives exactly

`R_j ≤ exp(−2x²−log(y)) = (j/N) exp(−2x²)`.

After multiplying the endpoint rate CE beta/j, j cancels and produces CE beta/N exp(−2x²), uniformly in the complete suffix energy. The early W moment is bounded by 2CW/sqrt(n); summing over at most n ranks gives the stated early payment. This direct proof is valid independently of the original real-power summation, which is not used in the implementation.

Small j is handled before either strip head is invoked: the actual Cauchy argument forces j≥x²≥256 on every nonempty strip. For j<12 the set is empty. The actual early set uses the equivalent real inequality 160000j≤n directly, so there is no unproved floor conversion or a j=0 division. Here j=r+1≥1 throughout the rank sums.

## True-block disintegration and lower-wall transfer

The actual `hSplit` head is a measure-preserving map from the canonical unmasked iid law on Path n to the product of the first j and last n-j original coordinate laws. Its complete private type has no conditioning, crossing event, stopping, symmetry, or atomlessness premise. `hSplitSum` gives the exact sum/energy partition. The source explicitly proves reorder invariance of full sum and energy and rewrites remainingSum/remainingEnergy to these genuine suffix statistics.

`hReorderMap` uses canonical independent coordinate evaluations under P, with each evaluation's actual law rho, and the full uniform labeled permutation law. It yields `(revealLaw P).map randomReorder=P`. This is an unmasked pushforward. No cap, energy event, prior-hit event, or other source mark is asserted invariant or independent under that map.

The generic `hBlock` fixes an arbitrary nonnegative prefix integrand A(q,v), bounded by the signed record gap D_j(s•v), and a genuine suffix-only nonnegative integrable V. Its source proof establishes product integrability from the product majorant D_j(s•v)V(u), transfers the complete head/tail map, and applies actual Fubini with the entire true suffix fixed. The prefix estimate is required uniformly for every nonnegative q and is then applied to q=energy(u). The law is the original product; the source masks have already been dominated pointwise. The measurability of A as a function of both complete blocks is proved in each application.

The lower-wall route defines eta(s)=map(z↦sz)rho and signLaw(s,j)=eta(s)^j. It explicitly transfers support, mean zero, second moment one and the actual third absolute moment for s=±1. `hSignMap` and `hSignIntegral` push only the prefix from rho^j to eta(s)^j. The fixed suffix remains an original rho block. That is sufficient because the prefix estimates are uniform over their law and q, and the suffix weights retain their original law. No symmetry of rho or invariance of nu is used. Energy of a signed prefix is explicitly unchanged for s=±1, and `hActualStrip` identifies the resulting floored strip with the actual source strip on Q≥n/2.

The signed prefix record gap is genuinely integrable on its finite support box. The source's coarser bound jBcap suffices, including j=0; no rate is obtained from that coarse bound. The W/future integrability and pointwise nonnegativity come from the exact accepted heads and explicit gates.

## Ordinary, early and low-energy payments

The actual ordinary source is the sum of both nonnegative halfline separated sources for the same arbitrary nu. `hCapRestriction` follows directly from the exact source definition: cap dependence is only r<cap. `hCapMono` then uses the accepted global halfline nonnegativity. Thus low(nu)≤lowKappa pointwise for every path, without stopping or permutation invariance. The accepted LowFullEnergy theorem's exact low-Q kappa bill and exp(−2x²) payment match the source's lowKappa definition. Equality Q=n/2 stays in the high branch.

`hActualEnvDom` converts actual record increments and future weights to the true-block envelope on high Q, then drops the high-Q and cap/source masks through a nonnegative pointwise bound. Its E, D, W values retain the correct closed endpoints and actual energy floor. Only afterward are the full reorder pushforward and unmasked block product used.

For late j, n<160000j gives 1/j≤160000/n. W's first moment and nonnegative full sum are used literally, including W_0=0. Fin.revPerm provides an exact bijection r↦n−(r+1), and the source proves the cast/subtraction facts where needed. No length-dependent factor survives beta/n times sqrt(n)=delta. The all-rank combined ordinary payment is bounded by

`CO = CL + CEarly + 1920000 CU CW + 1`, with `CEarly=24 CE CW`.

The coefficients account for 6 in the envelope and both halfline sums. The common base=low+earlyHigh pays all such ranks before any activity mark is imposed, by `(CL+CEarly)delta exp(−2x²)`. `hBaseDom` is a complete pointwise decomposition: on high Q it partitions the finite rank set into early/late; on low Q it pays every rank by ordinary and adds a nonnegative late remainder. This is an upper bound, so overlap with a later tail bill is harmless.

## Weighted prior-hit payment and explicit constants

The implementation preserves theta=2x/sqrt(n), support guard theta B≤1/100, and uses the weighted strip only in the large branch x≥400 and late j. Then theta sqrt(j/4)=x sqrt(j/n)≥1, as proved from n<160000j. Nonempty strips already satisfy j≥256, so the length guard is also met. The compact x≤400 branch is paid entirely by ordinary≤CO delta and the actual positive antitone tail value Psi(400); it introduces no fixed-level theorem.

The actual prior envelope requires the correct circular witness on the signed prefix. The wall lower bound gives witnessLevel=3x sqrt(n/2). APrior retains the closed strip and weak witness threshold, so equality atoms are not lost. The exponential majorant follows from exp(theta(L−witnessLevel))≥1, and WRS is used with the exact coefficient 253/500, fifth-degree factor and cubic/support errors.

The rational floor comparison `(88/125)sqrt(n)≤sqrt(n/2)` is valid because (88/125)²≤1/2. It gives theta*witnessLevel≥(528/125)x². The quadratic contribution is ≤(253/125)x², leaving exactly −(11/5)x². The cubic term is ≤8CWRS using delta*x³≤1, derived from the actual residual guard; the support term is ≤CWRS/100. Thus priorFactor is the exact nonnegative function recorded in the source, and each late prefix payment is uniformly bounded.

The complete `actual_circular_witness_small_parameter_moment` interface is additionally consumed only to supply unconditional measurability of the actual circular witness. Its numerical CMoment is not smuggled into a law-dependent public rate, and no circular-moment estimate replaces the required weighted record strip.

The late sum yields 160000 CWRS CW delta priorFactor per wall, 320000 for both walls, and the outer envelope contributes 6. The actual polynomial comparison proves `(1+2x)^5 exp(−11x²/5)≤3Psi(x)` for x≥16. This produces the exact 5760000 weighted coefficient in

`CP = CO/Psi(400) + 3(CL+CEarly) + 5760000 CWRS CW exp(8CWRS+CWRS/100) + 1`.

All constants are chosen before rho, n, x, cap and Brownian realization in the positive-budget construction. The compact reciprocal Psi(400) is finite and numerical. Its size is irrelevant to this existence statement.

## Weak-bad payment and legitimate omitted tail

The actual H=(2^64)beta²(1+x)^6, m=ceil(H), h0=4beta², kappa and tau agree exactly with the rare and omitted heads. The p=2 rare head supplies h0≤H/2, m≥4, m≤n/4, true future integrability and the rate only for t≥m. The source derives m≤n and tau≤kappa without replacing natural subtraction or introducing an auxiliary law.

`lam=min(nu,tau)` is measurable in every fixed permutation section. `hBeforeTau` proves exact equality of the original source restricted to r<tau and the lam source, for every domain and arbitrary cap. `hBeforeBadEnvelope` invokes the accepted deleted-label deterministic envelope at that lam; it retains the weak actual Bad mark and the exact record strip. `hBadFuture` rewrites the accepted remaining-statistic weight to the true suffix and explicitly separates its m≤t gate.

VFuture(t) is zero unless m≤t, so the rare estimate is never extrapolated to shorter lengths. The threshold sqrt(9x²/4−1) is the exact weak threshold, algebraically matching the accepted deleted-coordinate head. The source proves future/VFuture measurability, L1 and nonnegativity. It converts t^(-1/2) to 1/sqrt(t) with the correct nonnegative domain guard, then proves the finite harmonic estimate by telescoping square-root increments. The t=0 totalized reciprocal is zero; independently, VFuture_0 is excluded by m≥4. No bad-grid contribution is silently omitted.

The rare late sum is 320000 CU CR delta Psi per wall, 640000 for both, and the actual source envelope multiplies by 6. The early/low base is paid by the same unconditional bill. For after tau, `hTailRank` uses nu≤kappa and cap monotonicity; at r≥kappa it explicitly proves the nu source zero. The resulting sum is exactly confined to tau≤r<kappa. intervalPositive and intervalAbsolute are the same nonnegative components as the accepted omitted theorem's totalCost. Its direct rate CT delta Psi is used only on that legitimate window.

`hBadDom` separates r<tau from r≥tau on each late high-Q rank and then enlarges the late tail subset to the complete nonnegative tailNu bill. This yields the correct

`CB = 3(CL+CEarly) + 3840000 CU CR + CT + 1`.

The construction does not condition on the random value tau, assert it is independent of suffix coordinates, or use its omitted tail estimate to pay a prefix.

## Actual signed assembly, Gaussian comparisons, and L1

The assembly uses the same actual Brownian bridge Q and actualDerivativeFamily throughout. Actual halfline reflection and resolved interval spatial regularity supply measurable derivative data and KernelBounds; the actual source-parts theorem supplies real Bochner integrability. Finite discrete permutation sections are assembled into global measurability. Every application of integral_mono/Fubini/finite-sum integration has a supplied integrable majorant or accepted L1 conclusion.

The exact three-bill classification gives pointwise nonnegativity for every path. Its regular bill is CK exp(−x²)ordinary. Strict Bad is enlarged to weak Bad only on nonnegative U,L,max(−I,0). The interval negative bill matches `actualBadIntervalNegativeBill Q x nu` literally, and support100 follows from support200 with x>0. Negating strict prefixAlive conditions gives exactly the weak oppositePrefixHit predicates, including equality and time zero. The source proves these equivalences rather than assuming sign symmetry.

The private `density_formula` selected by the two run_tac blocks is the unchanged accepted Gaussian identity `(sqrt(2pi))^(-1) exp(−x²/2)`. The private head/tail selections similarly refer to the exact additionally reviewed interfaces. These metaprograms only add references to existing proof constants through elaborated `have` terms; they do not assert new axioms, run a mathematical decision procedure, or change the statement. Their actual name resolution/elaboration still needs the server kernel gate and is not certified here.

The explicit Gaussian lower comparison uses sqrt(2pi)≤3 and the accepted lower Mills bound. It proves exp(−x²)≤3Psi(x), exp(−2x²)≤3Psi(x), and the required fifth-degree exponential comparison. For the polynomial bound, `(1+x)(1+2x)^5≤32(1+x)^6≤exp(32+6x)`, while `32+6x−(17/10)x²≤0` for x≥16. This is a correct numerical absorption and uses a lower bound on Psi in the needed direction.

The final public constant is `3 CK CO + CP + CB + CN`, positive and universal. Both CP and CB already pay combined upper/lower bills, so no missing factor of two remains in this assembly. The final interval-negative contribution is retained and paid rather than canceled or dominated by a false absolute interval/one-wall bound.

All boundary cases were checked in the actual implementation: j=r+1 with r=0; j=n/t=0; potentially empty early/late sets; arbitrary small n subject to the assumptions; Q=0; Q=n/2; U=0 and the weak energy gates; equality crossing; closed strip endpoints and atoms; weak prior hits; strict/weak Bad; nonsymmetric rho; and arbitrary non-stopping/non-invariant caps. Each is covered by an explicit zero branch, deterministic empty-strip argument, exact source gate or nonnegative finite-sum bound.

The number 90 is only a textual coverage count. It is not an actual-owned constant inventory and cannot stand in for TYPE/FULLVALUE/AX traversal of a successful original object.
